newsitem.title: CANADA: Falconbridge loses cobalt to theft.
newsitem.headline: Falconbridge loses cobalt to theft.

text.p: Falconbridge Ltd said on Monday that thieves made of with 10 tonnes of its cobalt stored in Rotterdam, The Netherlands.

The metal was stolen the week before last and is worth almost US$500,000, Shelton Yip, Falconbridge's director of market research, said in an interview. The company's inventory of cobalt is lower than normal, he added.
"If we're tight in anything it would be cobalt," Yip said, but noted that Falconbridge has not halted supplies to customers.
Demand for Falconbridge nickel has picked up in the past week but has not cut into the company's inventory levels, Yip said.
"There has been a pickup in demand very recently, partly because of the price drop last week," said Yip, adding that customers saw the dip in nickel prices as a good buying opportunity.
Last week nickel prices plunged to their lowest levels in two years as stocks rose. On November 18, nickel was US$6,620 a tonne, but had risen to US$6,805 by Monday.
